items.name: Ballymore subsea tieback, Gulf of America
items.claim: Chevron's Ballymore project, a subsea tieback to the Blind Faith host platform, is expected to produce up to 75,000 gross barrels of oil per day through three wells.
items.source_excerpt: Ballymore is expected to produce up to 75,000 gross barrels of oil per day through three wells tied back three miles to the existing Chevron-operated Blind Faith facility.

items.name: Ballymore recoverable resources
items.claim: Estimated potentially recoverable resources at Ballymore are 150 million barrels of oil equivalent gross over the life of the project.
items.source_excerpt: Estimated potentially recoverable resources at Ballymore are 150 million barrels of oil equivalent gross over the life of the project.

notes: Ballymore started oil and natural gas production April 21, 2025, part of Chevron's goal to produce 300,000 net boe/d from the Gulf of America in 2026; Chevron U.S.A. operates with 60% working interest, TotalEnergies E&P USA holds the remaining 40%. The Gulf of America asset overview page (data/web/586b6cbc8fd4c0f3.json) corroborates the same Ballymore figures plus the separate Anchor project (75,000 gross bpd, up to 20K PSI, up to 30-year expected production) but is not cited separately here to avoid duplicating the Ballymore figures already sourced from the dedicated press release.
